milestones.title: Scientific Hybrid Graph RAG and RLM Navigation Base
milestones.vision: Evolve the M002 LadybugDB paper-level graph-vector foundation into a traceable scientific Hybrid Graph RAG base with PageIndex document navigation, chunk/claim/entity/evidence schema, hybrid retrieval baselines, evaluation metrics, DSPy typed extraction boundaries, and staged read-only RLM navigation workflows.
success_criteria: Fixture full-text ingestion can produce navigable PageIndexNode hierarchies with validation diagnostics.
SemanticChunk, Claim, ScientificEntity, ScientificRelation, and EvidencePath contracts exist and are test-covered.
LadybugDB stores the expanded SCI KG fixture schema idempotently and transaction-safely.
Hybrid retrieval returns traceable evidence paths with vector, graph, and fusion metadata.
Evaluation fixtures and ablation baselines exist before any scale or optimizer claims.
DSPy typed extraction boundary exists without premature optimizer use.
RLM document, workflow-in-code, and graph traversal modes are prototyped as read/draft-only capabilities with deterministic validation and benchmark comparison.

key_risks.risk: Overbuilding RLM before deterministic PageIndex and graph tools exist.
key_risks.whyItMatters: RLM without stable tools becomes untestable agent glue and cannot be benchmarked against cheaper baselines.

key_risks.risk: Hybrid retrieval claims without evidence-path evaluation.
key_risks.whyItMatters: The project needs trustworthy scientific and editorial evidence, not only similar chunks.

key_risks.risk: Full-text extraction quality may be poor for some arXiv PDFs or markdown conversions.
key_risks.whyItMatters: Bad structure will poison PageIndex, chunking, claim grounding, and later RLM navigation.

key_risks.risk: DSPy optimizers may be introduced before reviewed examples and metrics exist.
key_risks.whyItMatters: Optimizers without train/dev sets create false confidence rather than reliable extraction.

proof_strategy.riskOrUnknown: Can the project preserve full-text structure enough for evidence navigation?
proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: Fixture markdown/full text can produce navigable PageIndexNode hierarchy with ordering and provenance.

proof_strategy.riskOrUnknown: Can scientific claims/entities/relations be represented with traceable evidence?
proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: Typed models and fixtures preserve Paper -> section -> chunk -> claim/entity/relation/evidence paths.

proof_strategy.riskOrUnknown: Can LadybugDB support the expanded schema and hybrid retrieval boundary?
proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: Idempotent graph writes and vector/graph/fusion retrieval return traceable contexts.

proof_strategy.riskOrUnknown: Can retrieval and extraction quality be measured before scale claims?
proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: A benchmark fixture with ablations and expected evidence paths exists.

proof_strategy.riskOrUnknown: Can DSPy/RLM be integrated without becoming unbounded agent glue?
proof_strategy.whatWillBeProven: Typed read/draft-only modules and RLM tools return validated drafts and are compared to deterministic baselines.

milestones.verification_contract: Each slice must pass targeted tests plus Ruff, Pyrefly, Ty, and pytest before closure. Any real external-service smoke test must be explicit and must not hide failures behind broad skip blocks.
milestones.verification_integration: Integration proof must show Paper -> PageIndexNode -> SemanticChunk -> Claim/Entity/Relation -> EvidencePath stored in LadybugDB and consumed by hybrid retrieval.
milestones.verification_operational: Normal CI/local quality gates should not depend on live arXiv, PDF, or LLM services unless the test is explicitly a real smoke test with configured credentials and no broad silent skip.
milestones.verification_uat: A user can ask a fixture scientific question and receive traceable retrieved context with paper, section, chunk, claim/entity, score metadata, and evidence path.
definition_of_done: A fixture paper can be represented with PageIndexNode hierarchy, SemanticChunk records, Claim records, ScientificEntity records, relations, and EvidencePath traceability.
LadybugDB stores and queries the expanded SCI KG schema idempotently.
Hybrid retrieval returns grounded contexts with vector, graph, and fusion metadata plus evidence paths.
Evaluation fixtures compare vector-only, local graph expansion, heuristic traversal, and RLM-assisted traversal where applicable.
DSPy-compatible extraction contracts exist without premature optimizer use.
RLM spikes are read/draft-only and produce typed outputs plus trajectories, with deterministic validation outside RLM.
Full quality gates pass and no external service is required for normal tests except explicitly marked real smoke tests.
milestones.requirement_coverage: Covers R026-R035 as the primary milestone. Advances R017 from deferred M001 non-goal into a full-text prerequisite for PageIndex work. Keeps R025 BABOK deferred until SCI KG evidence paths exist. Respects R024 by keeping privacy/local-only optional for open scientific data.
milestones.boundary_map_markdown:
```text
In M003:
  Full-text and markdown ingestion contracts
  PageIndexNode hierarchy
  SemanticChunk, Claim, ScientificEntity, ScientificRelation, EvidencePath models
  LadybugDB schema expansion for scientific KG
  Hybrid retrieval baseline: vector + graph + RRF-style fusion
  Evaluation fixtures and ablation baselines
  DSPy-compatible typed extraction boundary
  RLM read/draft-only spikes for document navigation, workflow-in-code, and graph traversal

Out of M003:
  DSPy optimizer training with GEPA/MIPROv2 unless enough reviewed examples exist
  Production-scale corpus migration
  BestBlogs/social editorial product layer
  BABOK opportunity-analysis product layer
  Autopublishing or external channel delivery
  PyO3/Rust acceleration unless profiling proves a bottleneck
```

slices.title: Full text ingestion contract
slices.demo: After this: a representative paper fixture has stable full-text or markdown input, deterministic IDs, provenance, and parser fallbacks ready for PageIndex construction.
slices.goal: Define the full-text and markdown ingestion contract required for PageIndex and scientific evidence paths.
slices.success_criteria:
- Full-text/markdown fixture inputs are stored under deterministic test paths.
- Ingestion contract records paper id, source type, source path, text, provenance, and warnings.
- Poor or missing structure produces explicit fallback metadata rather than silent bad output.
- Normal tests do not require live PDF/network access.
slices.integration_closure: Connects existing paper artifacts to the future PageIndex and chunk pipeline without changing the daily cron contract.
slices.observability_impact: Records source path, extraction mode, parser warnings, and fallback reason for each full-text ingestion attempt.

slices.title: PageIndex document navigation
slices.demo: After this: a fixture paper can be navigated as an ordered PageIndexNode tree with parent child and NEXT links.
slices.goal: Implement the PageIndexNode hierarchy and navigation primitives for intra-paper structure.
slices.success_criteria:
- PageIndexNode records preserve title, level, order, parent, children, NEXT relation, and provenance.
- Tests can locate abstract, methods, results, limitations, and fallback sections in fixtures.
- Navigation returns stable Paper -> PageIndexNode paths.
- Structure-quality validation reports completeness/order issues.
slices.integration_closure: Provides the structural layer that SemanticChunk, Claim, EvidencePath, and RLM document navigation will consume.
slices.observability_impact: Exposes hierarchy completeness, section ordering, page/offset ranges where available, and parser fallback status.

slices.title: Semantic chunks and evidence paths
slices.demo: After this: PageIndex nodes can own SemanticChunk records and EvidencePath objects can point from paper to section to chunk.
slices.goal: Add SemanticChunk and EvidencePath models with deterministic IDs and traceability.
slices.success_criteria:
- SemanticChunk records attach to PageIndexNode.
- EvidencePath can represent Paper -> PageIndexNode -> SemanticChunk.
- Chunk IDs are deterministic and idempotent.
- Tests cover boundary ordering, empty sections, and malformed section fallbacks.
slices.integration_closure: Creates the evidence substrate for claims, retrieval contexts, and downstream editorial/opportunity layers.
slices.observability_impact: Records chunk boundaries, chunking strategy, token/character spans, and evidence-path validation errors.

slices.title: Claim entity relation contracts
slices.demo: After this: fixture text can produce typed Claim, ScientificEntity, and ScientificRelation drafts with confidence, provenance, and validation errors.
slices.goal: Define typed scientific extraction contracts before adding DSPy optimizers or RLM workflows.
slices.success_criteria:
- Claim, ScientificEntity, ScientificRelation, and extraction patch types exist.
- Drafts reference EvidencePath or explicit validation errors.
- Validators reject missing evidence, invalid relation endpoints, and unstable IDs.
- No optimizer or RLM is required for baseline tests.
slices.integration_closure: Supplies storage-ready drafts for LadybugDB schema expansion and deterministic validators.
slices.observability_impact: Extraction results include schema version, extractor version, confidence, evidence spans, and validation diagnostics.

slices.title: LadybugDB SCI KG schema expansion
slices.demo: After this: LadybugDB stores the expanded SCI KG fixture with Paper, PageIndexNode, SemanticChunk, Claim, ScientificEntity, EvidencePath, and relation edges idempotently.
slices.goal: Expand LadybugDB schema from paper-level foundation to scientific KG fixture schema.
slices.success_criteria:
- Schema includes required nodes and relations from R026.
- Idempotent ingest does not duplicate chunks, claims, entities, or relations.
- Writes remain transaction-safe and parameterized.
- Tests cover rollback and partial invalid patch rejection.
slices.integration_closure: Creates the graph substrate for hybrid retrieval and RLM graph traversal tools.
slices.observability_impact: Logs schema version, write transaction stage, merge counts, validation rejects, and rollback errors without secrets.

slices.title: Hybrid retrieval baseline
slices.demo: After this: a query over fixtures returns fused vector and graph results with evidence paths and score metadata.
slices.goal: Implement a hybrid retrieval baseline combining vector search, graph expansion, and RRF-style fusion.
slices.success_criteria:
- Vector-only retrieval returns chunk/claim candidates.
- Graph expansion retrieves entity/claim/paper neighborhoods.
- Fusion returns stable ordered results with score metadata.
- Retrieval output includes evidence paths.
- Tests include vector-only versus hybrid ablation.
slices.integration_closure: Provides the first grounded retrieval API for future answer synthesis and editorial layers.
slices.observability_impact: Returns retrieval mode, candidate source, vector score, graph score, fusion score, and evidence path for each result.

slices.title: Evaluation benchmark and ablations
slices.demo: After this: benchmark fixtures define expected claims, entities, evidence paths, and retrieval questions with metric calculations.
slices.goal: Create explicit evaluation fixtures and metrics before scaling or optimizer claims.
slices.success_criteria:
- Benchmark fixture includes at least several representative papers or paper sections.
- Expected evidence paths and retrieval questions are recorded.
- Metrics cover schema validity, evidence-path hit rate, retrieval recall, and groundedness proxy.
- Baselines include vector-only and hybrid retrieval.
slices.integration_closure: Blocks premature quality claims and provides baselines for DSPy/RLM comparisons.
slices.observability_impact: Stores metric definitions, fixture provenance, expected outputs, and ablation results.

slices.title: DSPy extraction boundary
slices.demo: After this: baseline extraction functions are wrapped in DSPy-compatible typed modules without changing storage schema or requiring optimizers.
slices.goal: Add the DSPy typed extraction boundary while avoiding premature GEPA or MIPROv2 optimization.
slices.success_criteria:
- DSPy-compatible Signatures or equivalent typed module boundaries exist for core extraction tasks.
- Outputs match existing extraction contracts.
- Cache/versioning policy is documented.
- Optimizer use is gated pending reviewed examples and metrics.
slices.proof_level: contract tests with mocked LM where needed
slices.integration_closure: Makes extraction contracts optimizable later without coupling storage to prompt strings.
slices.observability_impact: Records signature/schema version, module version, model name, cache key ingredients, and validation output.

slices.title: RLM document and workflow harness
slices.demo: After this: RLM can navigate a fixture PageIndex tree and run a read-only workflow-in-code extraction loop, returning a typed draft plus trajectory.
slices.goal: Prototype read/draft-only RLM document navigation and workflow-in-code over bounded tools.
slices.success_criteria:
- RLM tools are read-only and bounded.
- Document navigation can select relevant PageIndex nodes/chunks.
- Workflow-in-code can search/read/extract/validate over fixture data.
- Output is a typed draft patch validated by deterministic code.
- No direct LadybugDB write tool is exposed to RLM.
slices.integration_closure: Validates the first two RLM modes without giving RLM write access to LadybugDB.
slices.observability_impact: Persists or returns trajectory, tool calls, iteration count, subcall count, and validation result.

slices.title: RLM graph traversal spike
slices.demo: After this: RLM graph traversal is compared against vector-only, one-hop graph expansion, and heuristic BFS on scattered-evidence fixture questions.
slices.goal: Prototype adaptive graph traversal over LadybugDB tools behind a router and benchmark it against cheaper baselines.
slices.success_criteria:
- Graph traversal tools expose bounded neighbors, claims, entities, citations, communities, vector search, and rerank operations.
- Heuristic BFS baseline exists.
- RLM graph traversal is read/draft-only.
- Benchmark compares vector-only, one-hop graph expansion, heuristic BFS, and RLM traversal.
- Recommendation states when RLM should or should not be used.
slices.integration_closure: Validates the third RLM mode and decides when it is worth using versus deterministic retrieval.
slices.observability_impact: Records router decision, graph tools used, traversal path, cost/latency, candidate set, and evidence recall.
